record.paper_title: Problems and Conjectures in Matrix and Operator Inequalities
record.original_question: Under the same hypotheses that guarantee unitary matrices U and V with f(A+B)≤Uf(A)U*+Vf(B)V*, can one always strengthen that relation to a double inequality 0≤f(A+B)-Uf(A)U*≤Vf(B)V*? The question is asked for the same regimes mentioned in the source, namely the various conditions under which the one-sided inequality is known.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be a nonnegative concave function, and let $A,B$ be positive semidefinite matrices of the same finite size. It is known (Bourin–Uchiyama, and related results of Aujla–Bourin) that under such hypotheses there exist unitary matrices $U,V$ (depending on $A,B,f$) such that
$$f(A+B)\;\le\;Uf(A)U^{*}+Vf(B)V^{*}.$$
The question is whether this can always be strengthened to a two-sided inequality: do there exist unitary matrices $U,V$ such that
$$0\;\le\;f(A+B)-Uf(A)U^{*}\;\le\;Vf(B)V^{*}\,?$$
Equivalently, can one choose $U$ so that $Uf(A)U^{*}\le f(A+B)$ and simultaneously $f(A+B)-Uf(A)U^{*}\le Vf(B)V^{*}$ for some unitary $V$? Answer the question in each of the regimes for which the one-sided inequality is known (in particular for nonnegative concave $f$ on $[0,\infty)$, and the subcases of monotone concave $f$ with $f(0)\ge 0$, and operator concave $f$).
artifact.status_search_result: The strengthening to the two-sided inequality $0 \le f(A+B) - Uf(A)U^* \le Vf(B)V^*$ is posed as an open problem alongside the established one-sided Bourin–Uchiyama / Aujla–Bourin inequality. Searches surface related work on concavity matrix inequalities and Bourin-type questions, but no source confirming a complete resolution (positive or negative) of this two-sided strengthening in any of the standard regimes was located.

status_evidence.snippet: For nonnegative concave f on [0,∞) and positive semidefinite A,B, there exist unitaries U,V with f(A+B) ≤ Uf(A)U* + Vf(B)V*.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the one-sided inequality that the question seeks to strengthen.
